record.what_it_does: Cloud data platform for SQL analytics, data engineering, and AI workloads.
record.auth_notes: The SQL API and REST APIs support four methods: OAuth (Snowflake OAuth or External OAuth via Okta or Entra ID), key-pair JWT, programmatic access tokens (PATs), and workload identity federation (listed here as "other"). PATs are sent as Bearer tokens. By default a user needs a network policy before a PAT will authenticate. OAuth is the choice for multi-user agents, but each customer's account needs its own security integration.
record.access_notes: The 30-day free trial needs only an email. It can also end early if the free credit balance runs out. AI features stay disabled on self-service trials until a credit card is added. Continued use needs a paid, consumption-billed account. There is no permanent free tier. OAuth is configured per customer account through a security integration, so there is no central app review.
record.api_breadth_notes: The SQL API runs arbitrary SQL. The Snowflake REST APIs cover accounts, users, roles, grants, warehouses, databases, schemas, tables, views, stages, pipes, notebooks, Streamlit apps, compute pools and services, functions and procedures, network and password policies, secrets, alerts, Cortex Embed, Cortex Inference and Cortex Search, streams, tasks, integrations and tags. OpenAPI specs are published in the snowflake-rest-api-specs Git repo.
record.mcp_notes: The Snowflake-managed MCP server is at https://<account_url>/api/v2/databases/{database}/schemas/{schema}/mcp-servers/{name}. It accepts OAuth (Snowflake OAuth by default, or External OAuth) or a PAT as a Bearer token. The docs don't say whether it is GA or preview.
record.blocker_notes: Each account has its own hostname, so the toolkit must collect the account identifier for each user. OAuth needs an admin to create a security integration. PATs need a network policy by default. Free use is limited to a 30-day, credit-capped trial, with AI features gated behind adding a card. There is no event-subscription webhook API. Snowflake's own notification integrations and alerts only send messages a customer defines, so triggers would need polling.
